newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $64- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $64- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trading Wednesday was slow, with too few animals sold for an adequate market test, feedlot sources and USDA said.
About 900 head of steers and heifers sold in Kansas at $64.00 per cwt, USDA said. The sales were down $1.00 from Tuesday when the bulk of this week's cattle traded.
Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma feedlots reported 100 head of heifers sold at $64.00.
Kansas sales for the week as of mid-afternoon Wednesday were pegged at 77,800 head, including 18,200 contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.
Panhandle weekly sales as of mid-afternoon Wednesday were tabbed at 88,000 head including 27,100 head formulated cattle to be shipped this week, USDA said.
Feedlots remain very current in their marketings, with most of this week's showlists nearly sold, sources said.

Some packers requested early pickup of the cattle bought this week before a cold air mass sinks into the Plains late this week, cattle feeders said. The extreme cold could stress cattle and slow weight gains.
Low temperatures near zero Fahrenheit in the Panhandle and below-zero in western Kansas were forecast by the weekend.
